column1: # The expected divergence set of scripts/m_neutral.sh, read by that script and by nothing else.
# Key: fixture, level, class, separated by tabs, with the reason as a fourth field.
# A row without a reason is a parse error, not a row.
# Population. The fixtures are the 39 programs m_neutral.sh generates inline, named
# o1_a_vec_slice_write through o11_d_peeled_ref_no_field. No other name can appear here.
# That population is reproducible from any commit because the script carries its own
# corpus; it does not read the gitignored 449 file corpus and never has.
# Level is spelled O0, O1, O2 or O3, matching the O$level label compile_leg gives each leg.
# A bare 0, 1, 2 or 3 is rejected by the parser, so the two spellings cannot be mixed.
# Class is ir for a divergence between the two emitted prog.ll files, and text for a
# divergence between the two rejection messages. m_neutral.sh counts and asserts those two
# separately, so one fixture at one level can carry at most one row of each class.
# Only 16 of the 39 programs are accepted by the compiler, which is 64 accept legs over the
# 4 levels, and only an accept leg reaches the IR comparison. The other 23 are rejected at
# every level and can contribute text rows only. The class axis is partitioned by
# construction, not by convention.
# m_neutral.sh asserts set equality in both directions. A divergence that is not listed here
# fails the sweep, and a row listed here that is not observed fails it too, so a repair that
# silently removes a divergence cannot hide behind a list that only fails one way.
# The expected row count is pinned in m_neutral.sh as EXPECT_ALLOWLIST_ROWS and is 0. A
# missing, unreadable or unparseable file is a hard failure of the sweep; an empty read is
# not a pass.
# Measured at this revision with the compiler of this commit on both sides: 64 accept legs,
# 92 reject legs, IR_DIFF 0, TEXT_DIFF 0. There are no rows.
# Ten rows keyed to a different population were held here until this revision. They were
# produced by an ad hoc 449 by 3 corpus sweep that exists as no tracked script, not by
# m_neutral.sh, and no commit reproduces them. They are recorded in the claims file with
# their reasons verbatim.
